100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 18, 1926, the British Empire faced political tensions as Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin addressed the ongoing coal strike, which threatened to escalate nationwide. In Germany, the political landscape shifted with the rise of the Nazi Party, further complicating the Weimar Republic's stability. Meanwhile, in the United States, the stock market showed signs of volatility as investors reacted to economic uncertainties. Global unrest and labor disputes continued to dominate headlines, reflecting the turbulent post-war era.
